title: Attention Variants — Sliding Window, Sparse, Differential

questions.question: A long-context model’s full attention matrix is too expensive. What cost does full attention have in sequence length N?
options: Quadratic memory and compute
Constant memory and quadratic compute
Logarithmic memory and linear compute
Linear memory and constant compute
questions.explanation: Full self-attention scores every query-key pair, yielding an N×N score matrix and quadratic work in sequence length. Flash Attention avoids storing that whole matrix in high-bandwidth memory, but it does not remove the pairwise arithmetic.

questions.question: In code/main.py, window counts the total allowed positions. With causal SWA and window=1, which positions can a token attend to?
options: Every token within one position on either side
The previous position and its own
Its own position only
Every earlier position in the sequence
questions.explanation: The code sets each row’s lower bound to i−window+1. With window=1, that bound equals i, so only the current position remains unmasked; the prior position is excluded.

questions.question: How does sliding-window attention change memory and compute relative to full attention?
options: It scales with sequence length times window width
It scales quadratically with sequence length
It stays constant regardless of sequence length
It scales with window width squared only
questions.explanation: Each query in sliding-window attention scores at most W positions, so across N queries cost scales as N×W rather than comparing every pair. If W is fixed, this is linear in N; full attention is quadratic.

questions.question: What operation defines differential attention in this lesson?
options: Subtract λ times a second attention map from the first
Mask the first map and retain the second
Concatenate both maps before the value projection
Average two attention maps with equal weights
questions.explanation: Differential attention computes two normalized maps and combines them as A1−λA2 before applying values. Averaging maps equally cannot subtract a sink component, which is the purpose of the learned scaled subtraction.

questions.question: A long-context retrieval model loses useful distant information under pure SWA. What layer pattern does the lesson suggest?
options: Remove position information from the residual stream
Interleave local SWA layers with global layers
Use a smaller window in every attention layer
Replace all attention with a single local token
questions.explanation: Pure SWA restricts each layer to nearby tokens and can lose long-range retrieval. Interleaving occasional global-attention layers lets distant information be accessed while local layers retain lower-cost windows.

questions.question: A custom sparse layer should keep nearby context and some periodic distant tokens. Which mask pattern fits?
options: A fixed window that removes all distant context
Two independent softmax maps with subtraction
Local window plus every stride-th earlier token
A full global score matrix for every query
questions.explanation: The local-plus-strided pattern combines a dense nearby window with periodic links to earlier positions, preserving both local and distant context. A fixed window alone removes every distant position, so it cannot meet the requirement.
